prompt: Find the top 50 member-quarters by charge count. I want to see the member's first and last name, the statement number, the charge count, and the total charges.
gold_query: SELECT m.firstname, m.lastname, c.statement_no, COUNT(*) as charge_count, SUM(c.charge_amt) as total_charges FROM Credit.member m JOIN Credit.charge c ON m.member_no = c.member_no WHERE c.charge_amt != 0.01 AND c.charge_code != 'RF' GROUP BY m.member_no, m.firstname, m.lastname, c.statement_no ORDER BY charge_count DESC LIMIT 50

prompt: List countries by continent with their dominant languages where language percentage exceeds 90%, showing whether each language is official.
gold_query: SELECT co.Continent, co.Name as country, cl.Language, cl.Percentage, cl.IsOfficial FROM world.Country co JOIN world.CountryLanguage cl ON co.Code = cl.CountryCode WHERE cl.Percentage > 90
submitted_query:
SELECT Continent,
       CountryName AS Country,
       Language,
       IsOfficial,
       Percentage
FROM (
    SELECT c.Continent,
           c.Name AS CountryName,
           cl.Language,
           cl.IsOfficial,
           cl.Percentage,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.Code ORDER BY cl.Percentage DESC) AS rn
    FROM world.Country c
    JOIN world.CountryLanguage cl ON c.Code = cl.CountryCode
    WHERE cl.Percentage > 90
) sub
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY Continent, Country;

prompt: Identify the top 30 members (first, last) by cumulative lifetime charges.
gold_query: SELECT m.firstname, m.lastname, SUM(c.charge_amt) as lifetime_charges FROM Credit.member m JOIN Credit.charge c ON m.member_no = c.member_no WHERE c.charge_code != 'RF' AND c.charge_amt != 0.01 GROUP BY m.member_no, m.firstname, m.lastname ORDER BY lifetime_charges DESC LIMIT 30
submitted_query:
SELECT m.firstname, m.lastname,
       SUM(CASE WHEN c.charge_code = 'RF' THEN -c.charge_amt ELSE c.charge_amt END) AS total_lifetime_charges
FROM Credit.member AS m
JOIN Credit.charge AS c ON m.member_no = c.member_no
WHERE c.charge_amt <> 0.01  -- exclude test transactions
GROUP BY m.member_no, m.firstname, m.lastname
ORDER BY total_lifetime_charges DESC
LIMIT 30;

prompt: Find salary statistics for departments where salary statistics can be reported. Show me employee count and average salary by department name.
gold_query: SELECT d.dept_name, COUNT(DISTINCT e.emp_no) as employee_count, AVG(s.salary) as avg_salary FROM employee.dept_emp de JOIN employee.departments d ON de.dept_no = d.dept_no JOIN employee.employees e ON de.emp_no = e.emp_no JOIN employee.salaries s ON e.emp_no = s.emp_no WHERE de.to_date = '9999-01-01' AND s.to_date = '9999-01-01' GROUP BY d.dept_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT e.emp_no) >= 5
submitted_query:
WITH active_emp AS (
 SELECT s.emp_no, s.salary
 FROM employee.salaries s
 WHERE s.to_date = DATE '9999-01-01'
),
current_dept AS (
 SELECT de.emp_no, de.dept_no
 FROM employee.dept_emp de
 WHERE de.to_date = DATE '9999-01-01'
)
SELECT d.dept_name AS department_name,
       COUNT(a.emp_no) AS employee_count,
       AVG(a.salary) AS average_salary
FROM employee.departments d
JOIN current_dept cd ON cd.dept_no = d.dept_no
JOIN active_emp a ON a.emp_no = cd.emp_no
GROUP BY d.dept_name
HAVING COUNT(a.emp_no) >= 5
ORDER BY d.dept_name;

prompt: Find the top 30 constructors with the highest number of races where at least two cars started.
gold_query: SELECT c.name as constructor, COUNT(DISTINCT r1.raceId) as races_at_least_two_started FROM ErgastF1.results r1 JOIN ErgastF1.results r2 ON r1.raceId = r2.raceId AND r1.constructorId = r2.constructorId AND r1.resultId < r2.resultId JOIN ErgastF1.constructors c ON r1.constructorId = c.constructorId WHERE r1.grid > 0 AND r2.grid > 0 GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.name ORDER BY races_at_least_two_started DESC LIMIT 30
submitted_query:
WITH races_two AS (
    SELECT raceId
    FROM ErgastF1.results
    WHERE grid IS NOT NULL AND grid > 0
    GROUP BY raceId
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT driverId) >= 2
)

       COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) AS race_count

WHERE r.raceId IN (SELECT raceId FROM races_two)

prompt: Find the top 30 F1 drivers (first name and last name) by race completion rate, only including drivers with at least 50 race starts. Include total races, completed races, and completion rate.
gold_query: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, COUNT(*) as total_races, SUM(CASE WHEN r.position IS NOT NULL AND r.position > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as completed_races, CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN r.position IS NOT NULL AND r.position > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / COUNT(*) as completion_rate FROM ErgastF1.results r JOIN ErgastF1.drivers d ON r.driverId = d.driverId GROUP BY d.driverId, d.forename, d.surname HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50 ORDER BY completion_rate DESC LIMIT 30
submitted_query:
SELECT d.forename, d.surname,
       COUNT(*) AS total_races,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.status LIKE 'Finished%') AS completed_races,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.status LIKE 'Finished%') * 1.0 / COUNT(*) AS completion_rate
FROM ErgastF1.results r
JOIN ErgastF1.drivers d ON r.driverId = d.driverId
JOIN ErgastF1.status s ON r.statusId = s.statusId

HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50
ORDER BY completion_rate DESC, total_races DESC
LIMIT 30

    SELECT s.emp_no, s.salary
    FROM employee.salaries s
    JOIN (
        SELECT emp_no, MAX(to_date) AS max_to
        FROM employee.salaries
        GROUP BY emp_no
